principles: Current code and CLI facts outrank stale planning prose.
Review breadth must not weaken hard lifecycle gates or structured evidence requirements.
The story may optimize the target document but must not implement runtime or CLI behavior changes.
User-requested 3x2 review is valid for this story, while global host-default guidance must remain accurately described.
drivers: The target document is large and changes the future Proof-or-Stop flow.
The user requested 3x2 review and a final optimization table with reasons and evidence.
INIT product reviewer identified a medium advisory about Antigravity CLI default-host wording.
A document-only story should remain reviewable and rollback-safe.

options.name: A: Run this review as user-requested 3x2 with Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, and Antigravity CLI, while documenting that Agy is not the default primary host outside this explicit review.
pros: Matches the user request for 3x2 coverage
Keeps the host taxonomy memory accurate
Gives three independent host perspectives for a large document change
cons: Requires wording care so future readers do not infer Agy is always primary
May take longer than two-host review

options.name: B: Downgrade to Codex plus Claude only and treat Agy as fallback unless a host is unavailable.
pros: Matches default project memory for ordinary review work
cons: Does not satisfy the user-requested 3x2 review
Provides less independent coverage for a large planning document

options.name: C: Defer host review until after document edits and rely on ordinary REVIEW lanes only.
cons: Could allow evidence/role/routing mistakes to persist until later milestones

chosen: A: Run this review as user-requested 3x2 with Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, and Antigravity CLI, while documenting that Agy is not the default primary host outside this explicit review.
rationale: The user explicitly asked for a new story to review this large document and perform 3x2. The project memory warning is real, so the story should not rewrite global host policy; it should frame Agy as the explicit third host for this review campaign and keep default-routing language accurate.

preMortem.scenario: The 3x2 review output is treated as gate evidence by itself.
preMortem.trigger: The document says a host verdict or prompt prose passes a lifecycle gate without a structured CLI artifact.
preMortem.consequence: Future implementation could weaken REVIEW or DONE gates.
preMortem.mitigation: Require every accepted optimization to cite the structured writer/reader/gate boundary and preserve prompt-text-is-not-evidence language.

preMortem.scenario: The document accidentally makes Antigravity CLI a global primary host.
preMortem.trigger: 3x2 wording is copied into general routing guidance without the explicit-review qualifier.
preMortem.consequence: Future workflows may conflict with current default host policy and dev-memory guidance.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep Agy wording scoped to this review story or explicit 3x2 campaigns, and record the product-reviewer advisory in the optimization ledger.

preMortem.scenario: The review expands into CLI code changes.
preMortem.trigger: A finding says current implementation lacks a feature and the story starts patching packages/main.
preMortem.consequence: The document-review story violates scope and bypasses Proofbound code-change story discipline.
preMortem.mitigation: Treat code gaps as documented future implementation stories unless the user explicitly expands scope and a new story is created.

preMortem.scenario: The final table omits rejected or deferred suggestions.
preMortem.trigger: Only accepted edits are listed at DONE.
preMortem.consequence: Future implementers cannot see why advice was rejected or deferred.
preMortem.mitigation: The reconciliation ledger must include accept/reject/defer status with reason and evidence; the DONE table lists concrete optimizations made and notes linked deferred/rejected findings separately.
